author: thesamparr
text:
What's the greatest thing my parents gave me?

In 2011, I was a junior in college, I heard about an early stage company called Airbed and Breakfast (now called Airbnb).

I cold emailed the founder explaining why he should give me a job.

He asked if I lived in the Bay Area and if I would want to interview for a position.

I didn't even know what the Bay Area meant.

I was living in Nashville, Tennessee at the time and had never been to California.

But I said yes. I flew there Monday and got the job.

I came back to Nashville and called my parents (who lived in Missouri). I told them I was moving to SF in a few weeks to join a startup.

They didn't even know what a startup was (me either, really)! They thought it was a ponzi scheme. And I hadn't gotten a diploma yet (I eventually got it 6 months later).

Still, they said: alright, we'll come down and help you back.

Well, while they were helping me pack, we got a call from Airbnb.

I lied on the application. I said I didn't have a misdemeanor. I did. A recent DUI (I'm now sober). Airbnb found out.

So, literally the night before my flight, while out to eat with my parents, Airbnb called. "You're supposed to start next week...but we're rescinding our offer. You lied."

It was awful! But very fair of them.

Yet, my parents encouraged me to go to SF and make something happen. They gave me ~$5,000 as a gift and told me they know I'll figure it out. I didn't have a place to live or a job.
